paragraphs.text: A song of life soars over fields of blood.
If only every message were as perfect as its bearer.
Knights fight for honor and mercenaries fight for gold. The militia fights for hearth and home.
Just as each added feather steadies the wing, so does the flock grow stronger with each new member.
Even an enemy is a valuable resource.
"Their eyes will shrivel and blacken before faith's true light."
"Why do we pray to the Ancestor? Because She listens." —Mystic elder
"He can split a marshfly in two from halfway across the range." —Onean sergeant
To outrace the griffin —Kipamu expression meaning "to do the impossible"
They fletch their arrows with the feathers of angels.
"Precision is frequently more valuable than force."
Each victory adds a new verse.
The turning of the tide always begins with one soldier's decision to head back into the fray.
"The day of Spirits; my soul's calm retreat / Which none disturb!" —Henry Vaughan, "The Night"
"It is not a choice I make, to have this guard. It is the choice of my people, and my duty to them." —Oracle *en*-Vec
A fool knows no fear. A hero shows no fear.
Made from its wearer's hopes, the mask ensures that those hopes will be fulfilled.
A skilled decoy can throw your enemies off your trail. A master decoy can survive to do it again.
Her heart holds the pain of every soldier she's ever healed.
Fighting for the right reason is itself a source of strength.
The future isn't sacred, but its speaker is.
For the first time in his life, Grakk felt a little warm and fuzzy inside.
"We three, though of separate ancestry, join in brotherhood. . . . We dare not hope to be together always but hereby vow to die the selfsame day." —Peach Garden Oath
Some say they are the weapons of heroes fallen in battle, eager for one last chance at glory.
"Let me redeem my brothers both from death." —William Shakespeare, *Titus Andronicus*
"Trust me—the walls have more than just ears." —Orcish spy
The land will never betray those who gave their lives for it.
"Over the silver mountains, Where spring the nectar fountains, There will I kiss The bowl of bliss; And drink my everlasting fill. . . ." —Sir Walter Raleigh, "The Pilgrimage"
Healers ultimately acquire the divine gifts of spiritual and physical wholeness. The most devout are also granted the ability to pass physical wholeness on to others.
"The peasants labor for my profit. I approve."
Even the brave are scared by a lion three times: first by its tracks, again by its roar, and one last time face to face. —Somali proverb
She reads the battlefield like a map, always seeking the shortest route to victory.
When she flies above the good, they consider themselves blessed. When she flies above the wicked, they consider themselves dead.
"We must all hang together, or assuredly we shall all hang separately." —Benjamin Franklin
"I am bound to all my children. I share in their joys, I rage at their injuries."
The less you have, the harder you fight for it.
The key to winning any fight is simply staying alive.
Its eye the glaring sun, its cry the keening wind.
Sometimes the wings of fallen dragons refuse to give up the sky.
Most soldiers think of the sword as a weapon. In the hands of Zho monks, swords are also the strongest of shields.
"I heard their eerie howling, the wolves calling their kindred across the frozen plains." —Onean scout
Age wears the flesh but galvanizes the soul.
Sharper than wind, lighter than air.
"Believe in the ideal, not the idol." —Serra
Pray that it doesn't seek the safety of your lungs.
"Words—so innocent and powerless are they, as standing in a dictionary; how potent for good and evil they become to one who knows how to combine them!" —Nathaniel Hawthorne
The same spears that catch their food today will defend their homes tomorrow.
"To empty your mind is to fill your grave." —Lat-Nam teaching
"Returne from whence ye came. . . ." —Edmund Spenser, *The Faerie Queene*
In Mercadia City, loyalties extend only as far as your purse can stretch.
Though those who study are as many as the hairs on an ox, those who succeed are as rare as unicorns' horns. —Chinese proverb
Jamuraan farmers fear three things above all else: droughts, floods, and hornclaws.
"I don't like to think of myself as a pirate. I'm more like a stimulator of the local economy."
"The treasure in my mind is greater than any worldly glory."
"It is better to take what does not belong to you than to let it lie around neglected." —Mark Twain, *More Maxims of Mark*
Some fishers like to eat eels, and some eels like to eat fishers.
"Cowards die many times before their deaths; The valiant never taste of death but once." —William Shakespeare, *Julius Caesar*
"You know that secret? The one that wakes you up at night in a cold sweat? The one you think no one else in the world knows? Well, guess what."
"I've seen my master do this a hundred times. How hard can it be?"
The golden rule of revenge: Do unto others what they tried to do unto you.
"Cry to the sun and watch as even your tears forsake you." —Acolyte of Marit Lage
Which is more unsettling: the roar of battle or the silence that follows?
Scholars in their ivory towers call them "sharks of the sky." Scholars on the road don't call them at all.
"So much for that bright idea!"
"Beware lest you lose the substance by grasping at the shadow." —Aesop, *Fables*, trans. Jacobs
The College of Lat-Nam is often forced to expel students whose experiments grow too risky or too cruel.
The deep sleep of winter is not always restful.
It doesn't like having visitors . . . unless it's having them for lunch.
"Let's see . . . Mercadia, mercenary, merfolk . . . you know, I really need a better filing system."
Madness and genius are separated only by degrees of success.
One footstep among many is silent. One footstep alone is deafening.
Verick held his breath. Breathing wouldn't reveal his position, but it would force him to smell the goblins.
Of royal blood among the spirits of the air, the Mahamoti djinn rides on the wings of the winds. As dangerous in the gambling hall as he is in battle, he is a master of trickery and misdirection.
The fatal flaw in every plan is the assumption that you know more than your enemy.
To scrape out a living in Aphetto, wizards are reduced to selling rumors, lies, forgeries, or—if they get desperate enough—the truth.
Lat-Nam wizards trade knowledge on scrolls made of magic so they can better guard against thieves and spies.
It can pass through solid matter—but that doesn't mean it's harmless.
"Getting people to do what you want is merely a matter of telling them what they want to hear."
"Let's go over this one more time. . . ."
Within each device is a spark of its creator's soul. Within each sage is a lamp that awaits that spark.
It's easy to believe the monster is a myth—until you feel three hundred thousand pounds of myth crashing down on your ship.
Master the sky and you rule everything beneath it. —Metathran saying
Keep watch only for the giants and you'll be eaten by the ants.
It dodges waves of water to prepare for waves of magic.
Storm crow descending, winter unending. Storm crow departing, summer is starting.
"Secrets? What secrets?"
"Of course she's at the head of her class. All of her classmates have disappeared." —Tolarian renegade
Other birds collect twigs for their nests. Magpies steal jewels for theirs.
To merfolk, pirates are a nuisance. To pirates, merfolk are a threat. To the kraken, they're both appetizers.
The wise, the righteous, the mighty—the merchant feeds them all.
"Wealth means power; the power to subdue, to crush, to exploit, the power to enslave, to outrage, to degrade." —Emma Goldman, "Anarchism"
When no falcons fly, beware the sky. —Femeref aphorism
"But high she shoots through air and light, Above all low delay, Where nothing earthly bounds her flight, Nor shadow dims her way." —Thomas Moore, "Oh that I had Wings"
"Marit Lage lies frozen in a glacier's heart. Still her dreams take form in our world, stealing the heat from our souls." —Halvor Arenson, Kjeldoran priest
To gaze under its hood is to invite death.
"Knowledge demands sacrifice."
Think of it as a butcher knife with wings.
The bodies of its victims are the only tracks it leaves.
A wall built from the bodies of the enemy will never lack building material in times of war.
"Human tenderness is simply weakness in a pretty package."
"Ha, banishment? Be merciful, say 'death,' For exile hath more terror in his look, Much more than death." —William Shakespeare, *Romeo and Juliet*
"Kill them all and feed them to the new recruits." —Crovax, ascendant evincar
"Neither could I forget what I had read of these pits—that the *sudden* extinction of life formed no part of their most horrible plan." —Edgar Allan Poe, "The Pit and the Pendulum"
Your entire life passes before its eyes.
They feed on the living to stay undead.
The best ideas often come from the worst minds.
"The dead make good soldiers. They can't disobey orders, they never surrender, and they don't stop fighting when a random body part falls off." —Nevinyrral, *Necromancer's Handbook*
It despises humans and squirrels and beasts and dwarves and cephalids . . . well, it despises just about everything.
"There is no worse enemy. His passion for death doesn't just border on insanity, it wallows in it." —Southern paladin
"Any fool who would die for honor is better off dead." —Cabal Patriarch
"Why do you weep for the dead? I rejoice, for they have died for me."
"The horror! The horror!" —Joseph Conrad, *Heart of Darkness*
Toren had stepped on a lot of bugs during his life, so he couldn't help feeling embarrassed when a bug stepped on him.
Greed and gluttony led him to death. Now they are his greatest assets.
"The bonds of loyalty can tie one to the grave." —Crovax, ascendant evincar
A full coffin is like a full coffer—both are attractive to thieves.
Opportunity makes the thief. —Roman proverb
On darkness feeding, in nightmares breeding.
"I confer with Death itself. What could you possibly do to injure me?"
"We do not suddenly fall on death, but advance towards it by slight degrees; we die every day." —Seneca, *Epistles*, trans. Gummere
Memories cut from the mind can cut right back.
What wizards fear most is losing their minds.
"I can't think with all that screaming."
When you get into the swamp, the swamp gets into you.
Which hurts more: a sword in the gut or a dagger in the back?
No fear. No sense. And soon, no lunch.
The thunder of its hooves beats dreams into despair.
"Of all the tyrannies on humane kind The worst is that which persecutes the mind." —John Dryden, "The Hind and the Panther"
A drop of humanity for a sea of power.
"The final stage of the illness: delirium, convulsions, and death." —Phyrexian progress notes
No one knows whether they were named for the disease they carry or for the speed at which they multiply.
"The second wind of ascension is Reaver, slaying the unworthy." —*Keld Triumphant*
His mind, like his body, is made up of the swamp's flotsam.
The earth cannot hold that which magic commands.
Nothing is sacred to the rats. Everything is simply another meal.
Trained in the arts of stealth, royal assassins choose their victims carefully, relying on timing and precision rather than brute force.

"They groaned, they stirred, they all uprose, Nor spake, nor moved their eyes; It had been strange, even in a dream, To have seen those dead men rise." —Samuel Taylor Coleridge, "The Rime of the Ancient Mariner"
A hiss before dying.
"The mortal world is a grove of sweet fruit, and I am ready to harvest it." —Fallen angel
No one in Aphetto answers a knock at the door after sundown.
The elves had the edge in guile, skill, and valor. But in the end, only sheer numbers mattered.
You are who you eat.
What it lacks in backbone, it makes up for in cruelty.
"Rats, rats, rats! Hundreds, thousands, millions of them, and every one a life." —Bram Stoker, *Dracula*
"In the drowsy dark cave of the mind, dreams build their nest with fragments dropped from day's caravan." —Rabindranath Tagore
Such power grows the body as it shrinks the soul.
Only the most ravenous soul feeds on the health of the weak.
"The spirit of the devout is easily crushed by the loss of hope." —Fallen angel
"Expect nothing but scorn, flattery, and lies. And never turn your back on him." —Northern paladin
"The first birth celebrates life. The second birth mocks it." —Mystic elder
Just try taking *this* bull by the horns.
"From the snowy slopes of Kaelor, To the canyons of Bandu, We drink and fight and feast and die As we were born to do." —Balduvian tavern song
Fire never dies alone.
Heavy light flooded across the landscape, cloaking everything in deep crimson.
After their first encounter, the goblins named him Chuck.
"When every reef is bared and every wave is dust—only then shall I rest."
In the warrior kingdom of Keld, the cats used in the hunt are prized for their tracking sense and ability to climb walls.
"The smell of roasted flesh hung over the valley for hours." —Onean sergeant
"Pound the steel until it fits. Doesn't work? Bash to bits." —Dwarven forging song
Foolishly, Najib retreated to his castle at El-Abar; the next morning he was dead. In just one night, the dwarven forces had reduced the mighty walls to mere rubble.
"You wouldn't like me when I'm angry."
Dry grass is tinder before the spark.
The furnace awaits the next master who would stoke the fires of apocalypse.
The hardest part of his training is learning not to eat the boar.
"What's got two arms, one wing, and no brains?" —Ghitu riddle
To be king, Numsgil did in Blog, who did in Unkful, who did in Viddle, who did in Loll, who did in Alrok. . . .
He's smart for a goblin. He can do *two* things: hit *and* run.
Bent on a quest for blood, a giant can storm through a fort's wall as if it were nothing more than a picket fence.
Anyone can get around a cyclops, but few can stand in its way.
"Some have said there is no subtlety to destruction. You know what? They're dead." —Jaya Ballard, task mage
"Catch!"
"In some cultures, elephants are ridden by those in power. I don't think a mere elephant would even be noticed in Keld." —Onean sergeant
"Those who fear the darkness have never seen what the light can do." —Selenia, dark angel
"A flash of the lightning, a break of the wave, He passes from life to his rest in the grave." —William Knox, "Mortality"
Tortured with magic by their masters, the moggs are enflamed by the smell of sorcery.
"The enemy has been destroyed, sir. So have the forest, the city, your palace, your dog . . ." —Keldon soldier
Ogres learn how to smash stuff even before they learn how to walk.
"So they want to kill my men? Well two can play at that game." —General Khurzog
"You idiot! Never let the spies mingle with the orcish regulars after completing a mission. Now we'll never get them to fight!" —General Khurzog
Sometimes everyone decides to go for help at the same time.
"When the air burns, only death breathes deep." —Bogardan mage
"Who says lightning never strikes twice?" —Storm shaman
He raged at the world, at his family, at his life. But mostly he just raged.
"Be as fast as lightning, and you will be just as deadly." —Combat trainer
"Mercy? Mercy is for the playground, not the battleground."
While armies battled across Jamuraa, beasts stalked the high places looking for victims.
Called "stonefeathers" by many lowlanders, rukhs are thought to descend from a phoenix that sacrificed its flame for a body of stone.
To a sabretooth, all men are mice.
"The first wind of ascension is Forger, burning away impurity." —*Keld Triumphant*
Earth arms itself with fire.
The undisputed master of the mountains of Shiv.
"I love lightning! It's my best invention since the rock." —Toggo, goblin weaponsmith
War is a conflict that determines not who is right—but who is left.
"Of course you should fight fire with fire. You should fight *everything* with fire." —Jaya Ballard, task mage
Most people know better. Goblins only know bigger.
Where do you run when the earth becomes your enemy?
"Some believe sandstalkers to be illusions; those with scars know better." —*Zhalfirin Guide to the Desert*
Fire finds its form in the heat of the forge.

The ground itself lends its strength to these walls of living stone, which possess the stability of ancient mountains. These mighty bulwarks thwart ground-based troops, providing welcome relief for weary warriors who defend the land.
"There's never been a dwarven smith who could match the marvels that Gaea herself forges." —Elvish champion
From a whisper to a roar, the call is heard by all and refused by none.
It keeps the upper reaches of the forest free of every menace . . . except for the spider itself.
"One day we shall walk where once was water." —Eladamri, Lord of Leaves
"The beasts of the wild are my senses. It is through their eyes that all knowledge shall come to me."

The most terrifying thing about the craw wurm is probably the horrible crashing sound it makes as it speeds through the forest. This noise is so loud it echoes through the trees and seems to come from all directions at once.
Mold crept over the walls and into every crevice until the gleaming white stone strained and burst.
"For what are leaves but countless blades To fight a countless foe on high." —Elvish hymn
Each pluck of the strings breaks the hold of the unnatural on the world.
"Destruction is the work of an afternoon. Creation is the work of a lifetime."
From Gaea grew the world, and the world was silent. From Gaea grew the world's elves, and the world was silent no more. —Elvish teaching
"The stories tell of a distant time when machines overran the forests, destroying everything that lived. That time will not come again."
The king of Yavimaya's waters pays constant attention to his subjects . . . and thrives on their adulation.
Life is eternal. A lifetime is ephemeral.
"The love of nature . . . is a furious, burning, physical greed. . . ." —Mary Webb, *The House in Dormer Forest*
Five hundred years to grow—barely a minute to eat.
Rather than sheltering her young, the female fungusaur often injures her own offspring, thereby ensuring their rapid growth.
"It is useful to be able to speak to the trees. But it is truly wondrous to be able to listen to them."
The elves' battle cries cut paths through the Æther, guiding those who would stand in Gaea's defense.
Disturb a sleeping badger and the snapping of your bones will awaken the countryside.
Watching the spider's web —Llanowar expression meaning "focusing on the wrong thing"

Don't try to outrun one of Dominaria's grizzlies; it'll catch you, knock you down, and eat you. Of course, you could run up a tree. In that case you'll get a nice view before it knocks the tree down and eats you.
Sword hilts jut from some trolls' bodies where wounds healed so fast that the weapons were trapped inside.
Just one can feed a dozen people for a month.
"Ach! Hans, run! It's the lhurgoyf!" —Saffi Eriksdotter, last words
Some warriors walk the earth. Others are born of it.
"Most people can't build decent weapons out of stone or steel. Trust the elves to do it with only mud and vines." —Gerrard of the *Weatherlight*
A wolf without a pack is either a survivor or a brute.
"When the forest wants something, no mortal mind can resist her." —Maro
No two see the same Maro.
"Guess where I'm gonna plant this!"
Get in touch with your inner monster.
After the battle, an eerie silence gripped the forest. The losers' remains were lightly dusted with green.
Unanswered prayers are themselves answers. —Nantuko teaching
As long as the dryads are a part of the forest, the forest is a part of the army.
"One touch of nature makes the whole world kin." —William Shakespeare, *Troilus and Cressida*
The song of the forest is in perfect harmony. If a single note is out of place, the elves will find its source.
To renew the land, plow the land. To destroy the land, do nothing. —Druids' saying
It has germinated in the earth for thousands of years. Finally it wakes to the battle's call.
Nature grows solutions to her problems.
"Why should death always have the last word?" —Llanowar druid
Even what is lost beyond recall returns when coaxed by a dryad's hand.
To a dryad, every tree in the forest is both a doorway and a window.

"I wouldn't stand in front of that wurm, son. 'Course, I wouldn't stand behind it neither. In fact, standing anywhere near that wurm's not much of a plan. Running, now *that's* a plan!" —Wandering mage
Rain from this storm leaves you pinned to the ground like an insect.
Armodons are trained to step on things. Enemy things.
"Graceful? Yes. Beautiful? Absolutely. Harmless? Definitely not." —Fyndhorn elder
The sun breaks, the beasts stir, and the forest awakens to stand against its enemies.
Nature twists knots stronger than any rope.
"We are the hands of the great trees, reaching out to ensnare what threatens their branches." —Elvish hunter
Every branch a crossroads, every vine a swift steed.
Her roots connect her to the forest's wishes.
"A good lamp will light your way. A good ring will clear it." —Nervan, royal jeweler
The heavier the load, the harder it works.
"Hup, two, three, four, Dunno how to count no more." —Mogg march
Polished by a thousand waves.
"A good deal of tyranny goes by the name of protection." —Crystal Eastman, "Equality or Protection"
Legend has it that the world was hatched from a dingus egg.
"True power is controlling not only the hearts of your subjects, but their minds as well."
"The Eye altering alters all." —William Blake, "The Mental Traveller"
"Why build a bridge that needs to be guarded?" —Elvish champion
Woven from strands of griffin mane and pegasus tail.
Step 1: Find your cousin. Step 2: Get your cousin in the cannon. Step 3: Find another cousin.
Legend has it that the mine howls out the last words of those who died inside.
Forged by a thousand flames.
Blessed by a thousand prayers.
"Knowledge is power." —Sir Francis Bacon, *Meditationes Sacrae*
More than one mage has been driven insane by the sound of the millstone relentlessly grinding away.
Its wings were only designed to be ornamental, but it learned to use them on its own.
It doesn't think. It doesn't feel. It doesn't laugh or cry. All it does from dusk till dawn Is make the soldiers die. —Onean children's rhyme
These devices have been known to pull entire worlds through the Æther.
The rod is a relic from ancient times . . . cruel, vicious, mean-spirited times.
Though lifeless, the skull still possessed a strange power over the flow of magic.
Knowledge knows no bounds.
It doesn't point north. It points home.
Tainted by a thousand fears.
Urza protected his body well, but neglected his soul.
"A stick is your friend. A pointed stick is your good friend. An army of pointed sticks is your best friend." —Onean sergeant
Strengthened by a thousand limbs.
A beacon in the night, a dream in the fog.
The elfhames are the closest thing to "civilization" the elves allow themselves.
Only death breeds in stagnant water. —Urborg saying
Only the hardiest explorers survive to eat the fruit.
Deep in the heart of Urborg lie massive volcanoes whose thick black smoke covers the land with perpetual darkness.
"Training? Seeing my crops burnt to cinders was all the 'training' I needed."
Bitter as wormwood, sweet as mulled wine.

"Before my eyes was a horrible monster, worthy to figure in the legends of the marvellous. . . . Its eight arms, or rather feet, fixed to its head . . . were twice as long as its body, and were twisted like the furies' hair." —Jules Verne, *Twenty Thousand Leagues under the Sea*, trans. Lewis
Where air meets water, fish meets talon.
A bored wizard once created a vizzerdrix out of a bunny and a piranha. He never made *that* mistake again.
Its diet consists of fruits, plants, small woodland animals, large woodland animals, woodlands, fruit groves, fruit farmers, and small cities.
It does not wear a crown or sit on a throne of gold, but those who have witnessed its power hail it nonetheless.
